intelligence.enrichment: Earth takes nearly 365.25 days to revolve around the Sun, so the extra quarter-days add to about one full day every four years and solar calendars add a leap day to keep seasons aligned. Earth's revolution takes more than 365 days -> extra hours accumulate -> a leap day corrects the calendar's alignment with seasons. The learner correctly applies this rule: Earth takes nearly 365.25 days to revolve around the Sun, so the extra quarter-days add to about one full day every four years and solar calendars add a leap day to keep seasons aligned. Calendars have 365 days by rule, and leap years are arbitrary extra days rather than corrections for Earth's revolution.
